stories.title: Family returning from daughter's wedding killed in car crash:5 dead as Scorpio hits trailer; pet dog also dies
stories.summary: 5 people, including a couple and their son, were killed in a horrific road accident in Uttar Pradesh’s Mau early on Saturday. The family was returning to Gorakhpur in a Scorpio after their daughter’s wedding in Ranchi when the vehicle suddenly went out of control at around 3 am on the highway, broke through the divider and entered the opposite lane, where it collided head-on with an oncoming trailer. After the crash, the Scorpio was badly crushed and all occupants were trapped inside. Local residents and police somehow managed to pull them out, but by then all 5 had died. The accident took place under Doharighat police station limits. Preliminary investigation suggests the driver may have dozed off at the wheel. According to police, those killed were Vinay Srivastava (53), his wife Archana Srivastava (48), and their son Kritarth (27), all residents of Ranidiha in Gorakhpur. The two drivers — Nitish Kumar (20) and Purushottam Kumar (28) — were residents of Gaya in Bihar. Family was returning after daughter’s wedding Vinay Srivastava, a resident of Khorabar village in Gorakhpur, had travelled to Ranchi for the wedding of his daughter Vimansa, which took place on April 20. After the wedding ceremonies concluded, the family hired a Scorpio and left Ranchi for Gorakhpur — a journey of around 558 km — on April 24. Since the distance was long, two drivers were travelling with the family. After covering nearly 400 km, the vehicle had reached near Kusumha Basharatpur. At the time of the accident, Purushottam was driving, while Vinay Srivastava was seated beside him in the front passenger seat. On the middle seat were Archana, son Kritarth, and the family’s pet dog. The second driver, Nitish, was resting in the rear seat. Police said the vehicle was travelling at a speed of around 90 to 100 kmph at the time of the crash. Police suspect driver Purushottam nodded off briefly, causing the Scorpio to break through the divider and enter the opposite lane. A speeding trailer was coming from the other side, and the SUV was hit head-on. After the collision, the trailer dragged the Scorpio several metres. The trailer driver fled the spot after the accident. Vehicle cut open with gas cutter to recover bodies The impact of the collision was so severe that the sound was heard several kilometres away. Villagers from nearby areas rushed to the spot and informed police. Station House Officer Sanjay Kumar Tripathi reached the scene, but by then all five occupants had died. Police initially tried to pull the bodies out, but they were trapped so badly inside the mangled vehicle that rescue was impossible. A gas cutter and tractor were then brought in. The Scorpio was cut open with the gas cutter, and the tractor was used to pull it away from the trailer. Only then were the bodies recovered. The bodies were badly mutilated — some had crushed limbs, while in some cases faces were unrecognisable. Police have informed the family members.

stories.title: Father murders 3-year-old son in Jhansi, then dies by suicide:Child sleeping next to mother, taken away at night
stories.summary: In a shocking incident in Jhansi, a father allegedly slit the throat of his three-year-old son before dying by suicide. The child had been sleeping beside his mother when the accused, who returned late at night after attending a neighbour’s wedding, allegedly picked him up and took him into another room. Police said the man was under the influence of alcohol. He locked the room from inside and carried out the act. At around 2 am, when his wife woke up, she found the child missing. The room was locked from inside. When she looked through the window, she saw her son lying dead on the floor, while her husband was hanging inside the room. Family members rushed to the spot after being informed, and police were alerted. Police have taken both bodies into custody and started an investigation into the matter. The incident took place in Dhimpura village under Raksa police station limits.

stories.title: Shopkeeper burnt alive as fire breaks out in Kanpur market:5 including wife, daughter injured; firefighters rescue family with ladders
stories.summary: A massive fire broke out in three shops in Kanpur’s Dina Market in Ghatampur at around 3:30 am on Saturday, killing a shopkeeper after he was burnt alive, while five family members suffered burn injuries. Fire brigade personnel used ladders to rescue those trapped on the first floor, and five fire tenders have been battling the blaze for the past five hours. Preliminary investigation suggests the fire started in one of the shops due to a short circuit. Within minutes, the flames spread rapidly and engulfed all three shops, completely reducing the goods kept inside to ashes. The three shops belonged to brothers from the same family. The shops were on the ground floor, while 15 members of the three brothers’ families lived on the first floor above them. See pictures of the incident Family was asleep when fire broke out Three real brothers — Ramkishan, Satyanarayan and Rajjanlal, residents of Behta Buzurg — owned shops in Dina Market. One was a grocery shop, another a clothing shop, and the third a wholesale biscuit shop. Their home was built directly above the shops, and the family lived there. As usual, on Friday night, the three brothers shut their shops and went upstairs, where they had dinner with their respective families before going to sleep. On Saturday morning, locals noticed smoke billowing out from the shops and raised an alarm. Hearing the commotion, eldest brother Ramkishan (70) woke up. When he saw flames in the lower portion of the building, he moved towards a room to alert his son. At that moment, a thick cloud of smoke engulfed him, causing him to collapse unconscious. Moments later, he was surrounded by flames and died after being burnt alive. Fire personnel later recovered his body, which has now been sent for postmortem. In the incident, Ramkishan’s wife Gomti (66) and son Hariom (40), also known as Panak, suffered burns. Hariom’s wife Shreya and their four-month-old son Shivarth were also injured in the blaze. Ayushi, daughter of Ramkishan’s brother Satyanarayan, also sustained burn injuries. All five injured have been admitted to Ghatampur CHC for treatment. Five rescued through ladder operation All five injured were trapped on the first floor when the fire intensified. Fire brigade personnel mounted ladders and carried out a rescue operation to bring them out safely. Even hours after the blaze began, five fire engines remained at the spot trying to fully control the fire. ‘Before we could understand, the fire had reached our room’ Satyanarayan’s son Ankur said everything was reduced to ashes in the fire. He said the family was asleep when shouting outside woke them up. When they got up, they found the house filled with smoke. “Before we could understand anything, the fire had reached the room. Somehow, we ran and saved our lives,” he said. He added that his uncle died after being caught in the flames, while several other family members suffered burns. Tehsildar reaches spot, assures help As soon as information about the incident was received, Ghatampur Tehsildar Ankita Pathak reached the spot. She gathered details of the incident from the family and assured them of all possible assistance.

stories.title: ₹300 electricity bill rises to ₹60,000:Lucknow residents allege forced smart power meter installation
stories.summary: “My house has a solar panel installed, because of which my electricity bill earlier used to be around ₹300. But after a prepaid meter was installed, I suddenly received a bill of ₹60,000. I deposited ₹10,000, yet within just 15 days, only around ₹350 balance remained in my account.” Saying this, Yash Gupta, a resident of LDA Colony in Rajajipuram, demanded that the smart meter be replaced. In fact, electricity consumers in Lucknow have been continuously protesting against the forced installation of prepaid smart meters. More than 20 protests have been held in the city so far. Aggrieved consumers are surrounding councillors in protest. Consumers allege that even after depositing money, they are having to wait 5–6 hours — and in many cases an entire day — for electricity supply to be restored. A ground team visited to understand people’s problems. Here is what consumers had to say. See 3 pictures... Councillors surrounded; consumers say prepaid meters will not be accepted In Lucknow, consumers troubled by prepaid smart meters surrounded councillor Rahul Mishra in the Raja Bazar area. Distressed women consumers said that ever since prepaid meters were installed, readings have started showing higher consumption. Power cuts are happening at any time. Officials replaced the meters without any prior information, which they called wrong. Councillor Rahul Mishra said the public is suffering and officials are not paying attention to their complaints. He said authorities have been approached several times, but the problem remains unresolved. He demanded that smart meters be removed. Congress leader of the Municipal Councillors’ Group, Mamta Chaudhary, also raised the issue. Along with affected consumers from Habibnagar, Malviyanagar and Darugodam, she submitted a memorandum to the Superintending Engineer (Commercial, Central Zone). Mamta Chaudhary said complaints of incorrect billing have increased after the installation of smart meters. She alleged that these meters were installed forcibly. Officials had been instructed to install check meters, but despite that, consumers are getting no relief. She said officials have become unaccountable, ordinary people are not being heard, and the poor are facing increasing hardship. Memorandum submitted to local councillor on April 18 Women from Mankameshwar Ward had approached local councillor Ranjit Singh Yadav on Saturday with complaints regarding smart meters. The women said that since the installation of smart meters, electricity bills have increased sharply. Continuous negative balance readings are resulting in electricity disconnections. The councillor forwarded the complaint to MLA Neeraj Bora and assured action. He said problems have increased because of smart meters. Poor families are suffering. He also alleged that prepaid meters were converted from postpaid without informing consumers. Following this, MLA Neeraj Bora wrote a letter to the Energy Minister over the matter. Week-long protest at Laulai substation At Chinhat’s Laulai substation, electricity consumers staged continuous protests for a week. Residents of Kanshiram Awas Yojana alleged that 2,200 flats had their postpaid meters converted into prepaid meters without any prior notice. They said meter readings that used to be around ₹200 are now reaching ₹500, while electricity connections are being cut at any time without information. Local MLA Yogesh Shukla and councillor Mamta Rawat also joined the protest. The MLA visited the protest site more than twice and assured action. ‘First replace the meter, then we will talk’ Anger among residents of Indira Nagar was visible at the Sector-14 power house. On April 16, people gathered there and raised slogans against Madhyanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Limited, Energy Minister A.K. Sharma and departmental officials. After nearly an hour of protest at the power house, officials said they would inspect the problem. After this, officials walked nearly 1 km along with the protesting residents to their village. On the spot, people said that whenever they deposit a bill, it turns negative again within a short time. Following this, officials and staff checked the meters in the village. During this, women said the prepaid meters must first be replaced — only then would there be any further discussion. ‘We realised after three days that power had been cut’ Elderly Bachchi Devi, a resident of the KKC area, broke down in tears while narrating her ordeal at the 1912 control room complaint centre. She said she had been ill and could not deposit the electricity bill on time. According to her, power supply to her house remained cut for three days. After facing great difficulty, she came to know about it, following which she paid the bill. She said her bill was around ₹1,000, which she has now deposited. ‘A ₹60,000 bill came suddenly’ Yash Gupta said his household electricity consumption is 7–8 units, while the solar panel installed at his home generates up to 8 units of electricity. He said he is still being billed for that electricity, whereas the amount should instead be deducted. He demanded that a check meter be installed at his home. Women demand replacement of prepaid meters Lajjawati, a resident of Panditpurwa, said her smart meter should be removed immediately and the old meter reinstalled. She alleged that electricity department officials and employees pressured her household into forcibly installing a smart meter. “We are uneducated and could not properly understand what was being installed. Now we are receiving electricity bills of around ₹6,000 every month, which we cannot afford to pay,” she said, demanding that the meter be changed back to the old one. 'No hearing despite complaint' Soni Devi of Panditpurwa, who reached the Indira Nagar Sector-14 power house with her complaint, said her area is facing repeated power cuts, disrupting daily life. She added that despite frequent outages, money continues to be deducted through billing. “Even after complaints, nobody is listening. The meter should be changed. That is what we want,” she said.

In 2027, BJP should yearn for every single seat. 3. Mothers and daughters are unsafe under BJP rule PDA society now completely wants freedom from BJP. BJP does create narratives, but does not live up to the expectations of the public. Inflation has increased tremendously under BJP rule. All records of corruption have been broken. stories.title: Asha Bhosle’s granddaughter reveals her final wish:Immerses ashes with tearful eyes in Kashi; says, 'Grandmother will return'
stories.summary: Bollywood playback singer Asha Bhosle's son Anand Bhosle and granddaughter Zanai reached Varanasi on Monday. Both boarded a boat from Assi Ghat. They immersed Asha Bhosle's ashes after reaching the middle of the Ganges. Zanai became emotional during the immersion of ashes. Tears started flowing from her eyes. Zanai said, “Grandmother had expressed her wish to immerse her ashes in Kashi before her death.” It may be noted that Asha Bhosle passed away on April 12 in Mumbai. Son said, ‘Mother had an unbreakable bond with Lord Shiva’ Son Anand Bhosle said, "Mother came to Kashi only once in her life, but she had an unbreakable bond with Lord Shiva. To fulfill her last wish, we have come here today with the ashes. We have also performed her pind daan (ritual offering). Earlier, Pindra MLA Awdhesh Singh had received the family members at Babatpur Airport at 9:30 AM. After the immersion of ashes, Anand Bhosle and daughter Janai rested at Taj Hotel. Then they left for Mumbai from here at 4 PM. Granddaughter made an emotional post on social media After Asha Bhosle's demise, Zanai Bhosle shared an emotional post on social media. She described her grandmother as her best friend and an important part of her life. Zanai wrote that now she doesn't understand with whom she will have morning tea or share jokes. She wrote that she believes her grandmother will always be with her and will return one day to embrace her again. She said that Asha Bhosle was not just a great artist, but for her, she was the identity of life and happiness. Read unheard stories related to Asha Bhosle's life Eloped and got married at the age of 16, relationship with sister deteriorated Asha Bhosle fell in love with her elder sister Lata's secretary Ganapat Rao Bhosle at just 16 years of age. Ganapat Rao was 15 years older. Asha knew that the family would not accept this relationship, so at the age of 16, she ran away from home and married Ganapat Rao. This decision brought her more troubles than happiness. After marriage, she did not receive good treatment from her husband and in-laws. Time passed and the bitterness in the relationship also increased. This relationship filled with suspicion and tension gave up after just a few years. Ganapat Rao threw her out of the house. At that time, Asha was with two children and was about to become a mother of a third child. Out of compulsion, she had to return to her maternal home. In the year 1960, both separated. RD Burman's mother had said, if you want to marry Asha, you will have to go over my dead body After divorcing Ganpat Rao, RD Burman came into Asha Bhosle's life as a companion. The two met in 1966 when they were working together in Teesri Manzil. Both lent their voices to O Haseena Zulfon Wali... and O Mere Sona Re Sona Re. RD Burman wanted to do something different from his father SD Burman's legacy. While bringing the trend of jazz and cabaret, he found support in Asha Bhosle's voice. Both created songs like Piya Tu Ab To Aaja... and Dum Maro Dum..., which led to Asha Bhosle being called the Cabaret Queen. The professional relationship soon became a reason for growing closeness. Pancham Da was 6 years younger than Asha. He had divorced his first wife Rita in 1971. His marriage was mired in controversies. Due to increasing domestic disputes, he had left home and started living in a hotel. When he decided to marry Asha 9 years later, the family turned against him. His mother flatly refused. RD Burman's mother was so upset with their relationship that she clearly stated that as long as she was alive, the two could not get married, and if they wanted to go through with this marriage, Asha would have to enter the house by stepping over her mother's dead body. Hearing this, RD Burman left without saying anything. He wanted to get married, but due to his mother's displeasure, it was not possible. After a few years, RD Burman's mother became very ill and stopped recognizing anyone. After this, RD Burman and Asha got married in 1980. 14 years after marriage, RD Burman passed away in 1994. Asha was alone once again. Before RD's death, his financial condition was not good, due to which Asha and he used to live separately.

stories.title: Father enraged by daughter’s affair strangles her in car:Burns face with acid, and dumps body in Barabanki
stories.summary: A case of honor killing has come to light in Lucknow. A father, along with his friend, strangled his minor daughter to death. To hide her identity, the accused poured acid on the teenager's face. After the crime, the body was dumped by the roadside on Kursi Road in Barabanki. To conceal the incident, the father fabricated a false story about his daughter going missing. He also filed a complaint on the online public grievance portal (IGRS). However, the case appeared suspicious during police investigation, following which the father and his friend were arrested on Sunday. During interrogation, both confessed to their crime. The accused father stated that his daughter used to talk to several boys. In 2025, she had also eloped from home with a boy. He was angry about this matter. This incident is from Dhawa area under Chinhat police station jurisdiction. The deceased teenager has been identified as 16-year-old Vandana Chaubey. Now read the sequence of events... DCP East Dr. Diksha Sharma said- On April 16, Vijay Kumar Chaubey (34), a resident of Dhawa, Chinhat, had lodged a complaint on IGRS about his 16-year-old daughter Vandana going missing. Based on the complaint, Chinhat police reached his house on April 18, but Vijay Kumar was not found at home. Upon inquiring in the neighborhood, it was found that he himself had taken his daughter along with him. Police tried to contact Vijay Kumar over phone, but his number was switched off. Investigation revealed that Vandana had eloped with a boy in 2025. On this angle, the police reached the boy's house, he was found at home. He told that on April 13, he had spoken to Vandana on the phone. Vandana had said that she was going for exorcism with her father and he should not call her. After this, there was no contact with him. From here, the police's suspicion on the father deepened. Surveillance was taken help of. On April 19, Vijay Kumar's location was found at his in-laws' place in Gonda. The police caught him from there the same day. During interrogation, Vijay Kumar confessed to killing his daughter along with his friend Abdul Mannan (45). After this, the police also arrested Abdul Mannan. Read the father's confession… During interrogation, the accused father Vijay Kumar Chaubey revealed - his daughter Vandana Chaubey used to talk to several boys. In the year 2025, she had run away from home with a boy. A case was also registered in this matter at Chinhat police station. After about 15 days, the police recovered her and handed her over to the family. Even after this, Vandana was in constant contact with that boy. Angered by this, the father plotted the murder. On April 13, Vijay Kumar, along with his friend Abdul Mannan, rented a car. He took his daughter to Barabanki on the pretext of exorcism. On the way, he stopped at a dhaba at night. The next day, on April 14, he took Vandana in the car to near Sharda Canal, Kursi Road in the Baddupur area of Barabanki. He murdered his daughter, who was sleeping in the car, by strangulating her. Vandana resisted, but Vijay Kumar and his friend Mannan kept pressing her throat until she died. After the murder, they tried to throw the body in the canal, but seeing people moving around, the accused got scared. After this, to destroy identification, they burned Vandana's face with acid and threw the body by the roadside and fled. Body was found in Barabanki, could not be identified DCP East Dr. Diksha Sharma said - After accused Vijay Kumar Chaubey confessed to the crime, Barabanki police was contacted. Vandana's photograph was sent to them. Barabanki police confirmed that on April 15, a girl's body was found near Sharda canal at Baddupur, Kursi Road. Attempts were made to identify the body, but were unsuccessful. After that, after waiting for three days, a postmortem was conducted as unidentified and the last rites were performed. Dr. Diksha Sharma said that now Chinhat police station and Barabanki police are taking the postmortem report and other evidence to proceed with further legal action.

stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:Rampur court upholds 7-year sentence for Azam Khan son Abdullah; Munir calls peace talks 'tough' if Hormuz blockade continues and more
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. Munir tells Trump talks with Iran will be tough if Hormuz blockade continues US President Donald Trump and the Pakistani Army chief Asim Munir had a telephonic conversation on Monday. Asim Munir told Trump that if the ban on Hormuz continues, the talks with Iran will not be able to move forward. 2. Yogi cabinet expansion within 20 days, before 10 May: Focus on Brahmin, Dalit and women representation The Yogi Adityanath government plans to complete its cabinet expansion by May 10. Meanwhile, the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) is restructuring the state organization as part of preparations for the 2027 Assembly elections. 3. Rampur court upholds 7-year sentence: Azam Khan, son Abdullah convicted in PAN card case filed by BJP leader SP leader Azam Khan and his son Abdullah Azam have been sentenced to seven years each. The Rampur court delivered this verdict in two separate cases related to PAN card fraud. Earlier, the MP-MLA court had also sentenced both to seven years. Azam and his son had appealed against this in the Sessions Court. 4. Mallikarjun Kharge calls PM Modi ‘jhuton ka sardar’ Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said in Cooch Behar, West Bengal, that Narendra Modi is the “jhuton ka sardar” and that he lies to win elections. 5. Mother performs last rites of twin daughters alone: Father arrested after confessing brutal murder at home A father in Kanpur has been arrested for brutally killing his 11-year-old twin daughters by slitting their throats. The accused, Shashi Ranjan Mishra, is now behind bars after the horrific incident that took place in Kidaiv Nagar. 6. MBBS students severely beat 'mentally ill' patient: Gorakhpur’s BRD Medical College student alleges objectionable remark on attire by patient At BRD Medical College in Gorakhpur, MBBS students allegedly beat up a 'mentally ill' patient. The patient is said to have come out of his ward and reached near Sarojini Hostel. There, he reportedly made a comment on the clothing of a student passing by. 7. 21 dead as bus falls into gorge in JK's Udhampur A bus fell about 100 feet off the road on Monday morning in JK's Udhampur region. 21 people were killed in the accident, while more than 29 passengers were injured. 8. UP govt transfers 40 IAS officers, 15 DMs: Shifts Kinjal Singh to education dept after face-off with minister The Yogi Adityanath-led Uttar Pradesh government carried out a major administrative reshuffle late Sunday night, transferring 40 IAS officers, including 12 women officers, and changing postings across several key departments and districts. The exercise, finalized after prolonged internal deliberations within the state administration, also involved a large-scale reshuffle of District Magistrates (DMs) across 15 districts. Officials said the move aligns with administrative rotation norms and preparations ahead of future electoral requirements. 9. Yogi government eases rules for farmers: Wheat sale allowed at govt centres without registration requirement in UP The Yogi government has given major relief to wheat farmers in Uttar Pradesh. Farmers will now be able to sell their wheat produce at government procurement centres without a farmer registry. 10. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi gets emotional, KKR staff consoles teenager Vaibhav Sooryavanshi turned emotional after Rajasthan Royals’s narrow loss to Kolkata Knight Riders in IPL 2026, with a consoling gesture from KKR staff going viral. Meanwhile, Varun Chakaravarthy revealed players cried after KKR’s first win, highlighting intense emotions in both camps.

stories.title: High Court judge declines to hear Rahul Gandhi dual-citizenship case:Says, 'plea filed for political gain', cites misuse of court process
stories.summary: A major development emerged on Monday in the case related to Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's dual citizenship. Justice Subhash Vidyarthi of the Lucknow bench of Allahabad High Court has refused to hear the case. Justice Subhash Vidyarthi recused himself from hearing the case and declined to proceed further with it. The CJI UP will now have this matter heard before another bench. The court has ordered that the case file be presented before the Chief Justice so that a new bench can be constituted and further hearing can be scheduled. Took cognizance of social media comments It has been reported that Justice took this decision after taking cognizance of comments made on social media by petitioner S. Vignesh Shishir. Now the newly designated bench will conduct further hearing in this sensitive matter. Actually, this case was heard on April 17. In it, lawyers of the petitioner as well as the central and state governments were asked whether there was a need to issue a notice to Rahul Gandhi? The lawyers had stated that there was no need to issue any notice. Court reversed its own decision After this, an order to register an FIR was passed. The very next day on April 18, the court changed its own order to register an FIR against MP Rahul Gandhi. The court issued a new order on its website on Saturday, April 18. Justice Subhash Vidyarthi was hearing this case. He reviewed his decision before the FIR order was typed. In his study of old cases, he found that sending notices is necessary in such matters. The court said that it is not appropriate to make a decision without issuing a notice to Rahul Gandhi. After this, petitioner S. Vignesh Shishir wrote on X - I will complain about the case to the CJI. He had also accused the judge of taking bribes. Had ordered a CBI investigation The Lucknow bench of Allahabad High Court had ordered the registration of an FIR against Rahul Gandhi on Friday. Justice Subhash Vidyarthi had said - After registering the FIR, the case should be transferred to the CBI. However, before this, on January 28, 2026, the MP-MLA court had dismissed Vignesh Shishir's petition. The court had taken 'top secret' files from the ministry During the hearing, Judge Subhash Vidyarthi had directed the Foreigners Division of the Home Ministry to present all necessary documents related to the case. The ministry had submitted all files related to the case in the High Court. Vignesh Shishir claims that he presented documents and evidence in court. These indicate that Rahul Gandhi has been a voter in the United Kingdom. Records related to participation in elections there exist. On Friday's hearing, advocate Dr. BK Singh appeared on behalf of the UP government. The central government's case was presented by advocate SB Pandey. Bindeshwari Pandey appeared in court on behalf of petitioner Vignesh Shishir. Case was transferred from Raebareli to Lucknow Supreme Court had dismissed a similar petition in 2019 The Supreme Court had dismissed a petition related to Rahul's Indian citizenship in 2019. The then Chief Justice Ranjan Gogoi had said that if a company mentions Rahul Gandhi as a British citizen in a form, does that make him a British citizen just by doing so. CJI Gogoi, Justice Deepak Gupta and Justice Sanjeev Khanna's bench had said - 'We dismiss this petition. There is no basis in it.' The petition had stated, 'The court should direct the Home Ministry to take a quick decision on the complaint received about Rahul's citizenship.' The petition had also demanded that Rahul Gandhi be declared disqualified from contesting elections. Petitioner Jai Bhagwan Goyal had referred to the annual details of a British company for 2005-06. In this, Rahul was allegedly described as a British citizen. 3 cases against Rahul in UP Lost MP seat in Modi surname case Rahul Gandhi's membership was cancelled on 24 March 2023 after being convicted by a Gujarat court in the Modi surname case. During the hearing of this case, on 4 August, the Supreme Court stayed Rahul's conviction. Following this, the Lok Sabha Secretariat restored his membership on 7 August 2023.

stories.title: Rampur court upholds 7-year sentence:Azam Khan, son Abdullah convicted in PAN card case filed by BJP leader
stories.summary: SP leader Azam Khan and his son Abdullah Azam have been sentenced to seven years each. The Rampur court delivered this verdict in two separate cases related to PAN card fraud. Earlier, the MP-MLA court had also sentenced both to seven years. Azam and his son had appealed against this in the Sessions Court. The case dates back to 2019, when BJP leader and city MLA Akash Saxena filed a complaint at Kotwali Civil Lines. He had complained against Abdullah Azam for obtaining two PAN cards with different dates of birth. During investigation, Azam Khan's role also came to light, following which he too was made an accused. Read complete case in detail BJP leader and MLA Akash Saxena had filed a complaint at Kotwali Civil Lines on July 30, 2019. It was alleged that Abdullah Azam had violated rules by getting two PAN cards made. During the investigation, Mohammad Azam Khan's role also came to light in this case, after which he was also made an accused. Following this, a case was registered against both. According to the complainant - Abdullah Azam had obtained two PAN cards with different dates of birth using fake documents. In one of them, the date of birth was recorded as 01 January 1993 and in the other, the date of birth was recorded as 30 September 1990. Lower court pronounced sentence on November 17, 2025 After a long hearing, the Rampur MP-MLA Court convicted both on November 17, 2025. The court sentenced both to 7-7 years imprisonment and also imposed a fine of 50-50 thousand rupees each. Since the sentencing, both have been lodged in the district jail. Sentence challenged in Sessions Court The defense filed an appeal in the Sessions Court against the sentence. During the hearing, advocate Nasir Sultan along with other lawyers presented arguments from the defense side. From the prosecution side, ADGC Seema Rana and Additional Advocate General presented the government's case. The arguments from both sides concluded on April 6, 2026, and the court reserved its judgment and fixed April 20 as the date. Hearing also on demand to increase sentence This case has become even more important because a separate process is also underway regarding the demand to increase the sentence. Former minister Kazim Ali Khan alias Naveed Mian, who came second in the 2017 elections from the Swar-Tanda seat, had also filed an appeal demanding an increase in the sentence. Earlier, the Sessions Court had rejected the appeal to increase the sentence. In January 2026, the High Court was approached. The High Court directed a hearing on the appeal to increase the sentence. Under this order, a hearing is being held on this issue today as well.

stories.title: Yogi says, ‘Didi’s game is over this time':No cow slaughter, no Hindu divide in Bengal; supporters arrive with bulldozers at rally
stories.summary: In West Bengal, CM Yogi said TMC leaders are irritated by ‘Jai Shri Ram’ slogans and allegedly restrict Durga Puja and processions. Referring to Mamata Banerjee’s ‘Khela Hobe’ slogan, he said, “This time, the game will end and development will begin.” He added that cow slaughter and division among Hindus would not be allowed in the state. Yogi said in Bengali- Amar Sonar Bangla, TMC Mukto Bangla. Ondhokar Hotbe, Surjo Uthbo, Komol Khilbe. Boltano Dorkar, Chahi BJP Sorkar. (My beloved golden Bengal, TMC-free Bengal. Darkness will be removed, the sun will rise, the lotus will bloom. Change is necessary...we need BJP government.) The Chief Minister held a rally on Monday in the Pingla assembly constituency of West Midnapore district. While appealing to elect BJP candidates, CM Yogi targeted the Mamata government fiercely. To note, BJP supporters had arrived at the rally with bulldozers. When they arrived, slogans of 'Bulldozer Baba Zindabad' started echoing from the stage to the entire rally ground. Read CM Yogi's key points 1- CM said, ‘TMC cannot stop cow slaughter, this time Khela Band’ CM Yogi said, “TMC cannot stop cow slaughter in the name of appeasement. Cannot control the mafia. They are playing with security. They are stopping fencing on the Bangladesh border. For 15 years, hooliganism has been happening in Bengal.” “Before 2017, the situation in UP was similar. But after the double engine government came there, no curfew, no riots, everything is fine in UP. Now highways, metro, rapid rail are being built there. Bulldozers are used to break the ribs of mafias. Earlier lathis and bullets were fired at Ram devotees, now Ram devotees are honored,” he added. The CM said - Mamata Didi says, Khela Hobe. I say, “This time Khela ends, development begins. We will not let cows be slaughtered in Bengal, we will not let Hindus be divided.” 2. Broke the ribs of mafias with bulldozers CM Yogi said, “Here they don't allow Durga Puja, the government bans processions. Shobha Yatra is pelted with stones. Neither daughters are safe nor traders. This was the same situation in UP before 2017. There was hooliganism. Industries and businesses were ruined. Today there are no goons or mafias inside UP. Bulldozers are used in UP to break the ribs of mafias. There is no namaz on the streets. There are neither rioters nor those who slaughter cows. Here too, the BJP government can be the treatment for TMC goons who commit atrocities.” 3. Congress and INDIA alliance did nothing in 60 years Yogi said, "Farmers have done the work of growing gold in the soil. The tradition here has given new heights to the country's tribal culture. Saying Jai Johar to the tribal community on this land of Paschim Medinipur, I would like to say that for the first time a tribal woman has got the opportunity to sit on the highest post of the country. Congress and INDIA alliance ruled the country for 60 years but did not think anything for the tribal society. 4. Development happening in UP without discrimination CM Yogi said, “In UP, since 2017, every caste and class has been developing without discrimination. Our UP government does not discriminate on the basis of caste, religion or sect. If you want to see the model of 'Sabka Saath Sabka Vikas' (Everyone's Support, Everyone's Development), come to UP. There, every tribal person has received land deeds. They have their own house, their own land.” 5. Opposition snatched women's rights CM Yogi targeted the opposition over the Women's Reservation Amendment Bill not being passed in Parliament. He said, “You saw that they did not let the Women's Reservation Amendment Bill pass in Parliament. Insulting the poor, women, and backward classes has become their habit.” 6. We are proud that we are Hindus The Chief Minister said, “Bengal has been a spiritual land. This land has given birth to Ramakrishna, Lahiri Mahasaya, Swami Pranavananda and Swami Vivekananda. Vivekananda had said on the global platform, say with pride that we are Hindus. Bengal's youth were associated with Netaji and the Azad Hind Fauj. Congress insulted them.”

stories.title: Anushka and Virat visit Vrindavan ashram:Seek blessings from Premanand Maharaj on Akshaya Tritiya
stories.summary: Recent days have been a whirlwind for cricketer Virat Kohli and actress Anushka Sharma, filled with both online chatter and moments of togetherness. The couple, often admired for their strong bond, has been navigating the spotlight with grace. The week began with Virat finding himself at the center of a minor social media stir. He briefly liked a photo posted by German vlogger Lizlaz on Instagram, which became a quick point of discussion on social media. Virat-Anushka's first appearance after the fleeting moment Over the weekend, Virat and Anushka were spotted together at the Bengaluru airport, marking their first public appearance since the Instagram incident. Videos circulating on social media captured the couple exiting the airport. Virat sported a casual look with a black T-shirt and blue jeans, while Anushka looked elegant in a white floral kurta paired with palazzo pants and a green dupatta. One clip showed them sharing a lighthearted moment on an escalator, laughing and chatting. In another, Virat was seen carrying Anushka's bag, a sweet gesture that resonated with fans. Couple spotted outside the Vrindavan Ashram as they visited Premanand Maharaj Following their time in Bengaluru, Virat and Anushka were seen in Vrindavan, where they visited Premanand Govind Sharan Maharaj's Kelly Kunj Ashram. Their visit coincided with Akshaya Tritiya, an auspicious Hindu festival. Videos of their spiritual outing have since gone viral, highlighting the couple's devotion and interest in spiritual matters. Earlier also they had visited Premanand Maharaj many times This wasn't their first visit to the ashram. Virat and Anushka are known to be frequent visitors, often engaging in discussions with Premanand Govind Sharan Maharaj on topics ranging from life lessons and the importance of forgiveness to relationship advice and the nuances of marriage.

stories.title: Parshuram Jayanti procession turns tense in Meerut:Woman DSP warns of FIRs over carrying axes and sticks
stories.summary: In Meerut, during a procession on Sunday marking Parshuram Jayanti, a female Deputy Superintendent of Police (DSP) issued a strict warning to those carrying and waving farshas (symbolic axes) and sticks. DSP Suchita Singh used a public address system on the spot, warning that individuals carrying such items would be identified and cases would be registered against them. A video of the Deputy SP has also surfaced. In the video, the DSP is seen holding a mic and telling people- Those who are sitting on top, FIRs will be filed against all of them. I am telling you right now, those who are waving axes, waving sticks. Everyone is being photographed. Cases will be filed against all of them. Whatever sticks there are, separate them, get them separated. Her remarks have triggered anger among sections of the Brahmin community, with several people posting critical comments online and describing the action as anti-Brahmin. Procession taken out near Chaudhary Charan Singh University On Parshuram Jayanti, grand events and processions were organised by Brahmin organisations and other groups across Meerut district. The shaurya yatra (procession of valour) was flagged off from the CCSU gate and received grand welcomes at multiple locations. Youths participating in the procession were seen carrying symbolic farshas. The procession was passing in front of Chaudhary Charan Singh University on Garh Road when the incident took place. DSP Suchita Singh, deployed for duty at the procession, stopped the march near the CCSU gate and issued warnings through a microphone. Processions and rallies taken out across the city On Parshuram Jayanti, several processions and celebration events were organised across Meerut city and rural areas. At many locations, participants were seen carrying sticks and waving farshas as part of the symbolic procession. Axes waved in Delhi Road procession too A large procession was also taken out on Delhi Road in Partapur, where Minister of State Dr. Somendra Tomar attended as the chief guest. The procession also included a bulldozer display. Youths participating in the event were seen carrying swords, sticks, and farshas, showing symbolic strength. People said - This is a direct attack on faith Political reaction Rashtrawadi Navnirman Dal national president Shri Kant Tyagi said that a private programme planned in a school in Machhara, Kithaur, during Parshuram Jayanti was not allowed by the administration. The programme was to include distribution of stationery, uniforms, and prizes to school students. He said permission was denied on the grounds that it could disturb law and order. He further alleged that community members were being threatened and claimed that the incident reflects dissatisfaction of the current government towards Tyagi and Brahmin communities. stories.title: 'AMU is mini Pakistan, will slaughter bury you here':Doctor visiting AMU faces threats on campus; two students arrested after investigation
stories.summary: In Aligarh, two students who allegedly threatened a doctor by calling AMU a “Mini Pakistan” have been arrested. The doctor had gone to meet a friend studying BTech at AMU on 14 April when the incident took place. Allegation of mob intimidation and threats According to the complaint, the doctor was surrounded by a group of people after being stopped near the campus. It is alleged that the accused students also called a larger group, after which he was abused and intimidated. They allegedly threatened him, saying that AMU is a “Mini Pakistan”, and that he would be “slaughtered and buried there”. They also warned that his family would not even be able to trace him and that he would face serious consequences. Emergency call to 112 and police response Seeing himself surrounded, the doctor called the emergency helpline 112 seeking help. Police reached the spot shortly after and safely escorted him out after taking initial details. Based on the doctor’s complaint, a case was registered and an investigation was launched. Police examined CCTV footage and identified the accused students. Detailed account of incident The doctor, Kulwant Singh, said he is a resident of Nagalia Mev in Gajraula, Amroha. On 14 April, he had gone to AMU campus to meet a female friend. After meeting her, while he was leaving in an e-rickshaw, four youths allegedly confronted him and misbehaved. He further alleged that the group called around 30 people, after which he was abused and surrounded. A video of the incident was also recorded. One of the accused reportedly claimed to be an MTech second-year student during the confrontation. The doctor alleged that he was told the campus was dominated by one community and was repeatedly threatened with killing and burial. University intervention and police action AMU Proctorial team reached the spot and took the doctor to the proctor’s office for safety. His mobile phone was also briefly taken for inquiry purposes. Police from 112 later arrived and, after verification, ensured his safe exit from the campus. Arrest of accused students Police identified the accused as Shahbaz (MTech student from Ghazipur) and Najeeb (BTech student from Bareilly) through CCTV footage and investigation. SP City Aditya Bansal confirmed that after verification and coordination with the university proctorial team, both accused were arrested on Sunday evening from Suleman Hall and later sent to jail after questioning.

stories.summary: The Yogi government has given major relief to wheat farmers in Uttar Pradesh. Farmers will now be able to sell their wheat produce at government procurement centres without a farmer registry. The Chief Minister has directed all District Magistrates to implement this order with immediate effect. Special session of Assembly on April 30, government to bring censure motion against opposition Amid the Women’s Reservation Amendment Bill issue, the BJP has intensified its attack on opposition parties. In BJP-ruled states, special assembly sessions will be convened to pass censure motions against the opposition’s stand. In Uttar Pradesh as well, a special session of the state legislature has been scheduled for April 30. According to experts, members must be informed at least seven days in advance before calling a session. Therefore, the Yogi government approved the proposal on Sunday through a Cabinet by Circulation process. Cabinet by Circulation is a procedure in which cabinet proposals are approved without a formal meeting, by circulating them among ministers for approval.

stories.title: MBBS students severely beat 'mentally ill' patient:Gorakhpur’s BRD Medical College student alleges objectionable remark on attire by patient
stories.summary: At BRD Medical College in Gorakhpur, MBBS students allegedly beat up a 'mentally ill' patient. The patient is said to have come out of his ward and reached near Sarojini Hostel. There, he reportedly made a comment on the clothing of a student passing by. Taking action, the student called her MBBS friends. After this, the incident took place. The wife of the 'mentally ill' patient repeatedly said that her husband was not mentally stable. However, no one listened to her. Meanwhile, she recorded a video of the incident. Afterwards, students allegedly entered the ward and threatened her to delete the video. On receiving information, the Principal Medical Superintendent reached the spot and somehow brought the situation under control. Know the complete matter.… According to information, the husband of a staff nurse working at BRD Medical College was undergoing treatment in the mental health ward (old bed number 100). On Sunday, 19 April, the patient wandered out of the ward and reached in front of Sarojini Hostel. During this time, he allegedly made a comment on the clothing of a student passing by. Angered by this, the student called her fellow MBBS students. It is alleged that within a short time, the students reached the spot and thrashed the patient outside the hostel. No one listened to the wife The wife present at the spot continuously kept pleading the students, saying her husband was 'mentally ill' and requesting them not to beat him. However, no one paid attention to her. Meanwhile, she recorded the entire incident. Security rescued the patient After being informed, hospital security personnel reached the spot and rescued the patient, later admitting him back to the ward. It is also reported that after learning about the video recording, some students entered the ward and pressured the staff nurse to delete the video. After the matter came to light, the Principal Medical Superintendent reached the spot and brought the situation under control. stories.title: Landlord pressures woman for illicit relations in Lucknow:Harassment drives her to distress; husband leaves, leaving her with 3 children
stories.summary: In Lucknow’s Gudamba area, a woman living in a rented accommodation has alleged that her landlord molested her and repeatedly pressured her for an illicit relationship. The victim has filed a complaint at the police station, following which an FIR has been registered against the accused. Jumped over the wall and entered the room According to the victim, she had been living in the rented house for the past one year with her husband and three children. She alleged that the landlord, Vishal Rajput, started pressuring her for an illicit relationship soon after she began living there. She further alleged that on one occasion, when she was alone at home, the accused climbed over the wall and entered her room, where he forcibly grabbed her and molested her. Continued to pressure for months The woman stated that when she opposed the accused, he threatened and intimidated her. She alleged that this continued for several months, leaving her mentally disturbed. She added that after she informed her husband, Sri Ram Chauhan, about the matter, he left her. Since then, she has been living alone with her three minor children and is facing financial as well as social difficulties. Appealed to police for justice The victim has lodged a complaint at Gudamba police station seeking strict action against the accused. Police officials stated that an investigation is underway based on the complaint, and appropriate action will be taken after the inquiry is completed.

stories.title: New mortuary in Lucknow non-operational due to staff shortage:15 personnel required, postmortem process remains stuck despite 2024 handover
stories.summary: In Lucknow, families of the deceased are often forced to wait for long hours, sometimes even an entire day, for postmortem procedures to be completed. To ease this burden, a new mortuary was built at KGMU (King George’s Medical University) and handed over nearly two years ago in 2024. However, it has still not been made operational. The new mortuary requires at least 15 staff members along with equipment and other resources to function. This includes forensic experts, doctors, pharmacists, data entry operators, videographers and support staff. In March, the Directorate General of Health issued an order directing that all postmortem facilities in the state must be equipped with proper infrastructure and manpower as soon as possible. Official response on delay After the order, when asked whether the new postmortem house should now be functional, Chief Medical Officer of Lucknow, N.B. Singh, said that continuous meetings are being held regarding its operation. He added that the facility will soon start functioning with full manpower and equipment. Current condition of the old postmortem house Currently, the old postmortem house in Lucknow has only 12 employees, while at least four staff members are required per shift. At times, staff are also assigned to other duties, which further delays the postmortem process. Due to shortage of staff, bodies often remain waiting for hours before postmortem is conducted. 18 postmortems will be conducted simultaneously after becoming operational The existing mortuary has a capacity of 6 postmortem platforms. Once the new mortuary becomes operational, it will add 12 additional platforms, increasing the total capacity to 18 bodies at a time. At present, when the number of bodies increases, postmortems are delayed until space becomes available. Delay due to clash between CMO and KGMU It has been found that the delay is also due to a conflict between the CMO office and KGMU administration. Both departments are blaming each other, while neither is providing manpower. Although official orders are issued, implementation does not take place and the matter remains stuck. The new mortuary was handed over two years ago, but after repeated reports regarding its non-functioning, KGMU issued instructions on 24 November 2025 to arrange manpower and other requirements. However, even after five months, the situation has not changed and the matter remains pending. Deputy CM has also taken cognizance Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak had also taken cognizance of the issue on 27 June 2025. He directed that postmortems must be completed within a maximum of four hours. Following this, new arrangements were implemented across the state. He also instructed that in districts with higher workload, CMOs should form multiple medical teams to ensure timely completion of postmortems so that families do not have to wait longer for bodies. Key orders from health directorate Situation still unresolved Despite the infrastructure being ready, the new KGMU mortuary remains non-functional due to lack of manpower and administrative deadlock, continuing to cause distress and long delays for bereaved families in Lucknow.

stories.title: Husband sleeps while wife dies by suicide in Kanpur:Tragedy follows wedding celebration, discovered after child cries
stories.summary: In Kanpur’s Narwal police station area, a woman allegedly died by suicide late at night after hanging herself in the same room where her husband was sleeping. The incident took place in Panauri village. According to the husband, he was asleep when their young son, who was also sleeping in the same room, started crying. He woke up due to the child’s crying. When he called out to his wife and received no response, he switched on the light and found her body hanging from the ceiling fan. Shocked, he immediately dialled emergency number 112 and informed the police. After receiving the information, Narwal police station force along with a forensic team reached the spot. The body was taken down and sent for post-mortem examination. Police also seized the deceased woman’s mobile phone from the scene and sent the body for further procedure. Everyone had returned home late at night after attending a party The husband Deepak Singh, a private employee, said the family had returned late at night after attending a party — the wedding anniversary of his uncle’s son Mohit. He said all three — husband, wife Radha Singh (30), and their son — slept in the same room around 1 am after returning home. Deepak stated that later in the night, his wife woke up and allegedly hanged herself using a saree tied to the ceiling fan. He said the incident took place while they were asleep. In the early morning, their son cried, which woke him up. When he tried calling his wife and received no response, he turned on the light and saw her hanging. The family then immediately informed police by dialling 112. Police Station In-charge said- Narwal police station in-charge Anil Tomar said that no complaint has been received from the woman’s maternal side so far, nor have any allegations been made. He added that if any complaint is received or allegations are made, the matter will be investigated and necessary action will be taken accordingly.

stories.summary: A father in Kanpur has been arrested for brutally killing his 11-year-old twin daughters by slitting their throats. The accused, Shashi Ranjan Mishra, is now behind bars after the horrific incident that took place in Kidaiv Nagar. The twin sisters, Riddhi and Siddhi, born together, also left the world together. Their mother performed their last rites at a Hindu burial ground, where she broke down multiple times and fainted twice while holding the bodies. She kept crying over her daughters as no one was there to support her, until women police personnel intervened and comforted her. First understand the complete case Mixed sleeping pills in food, slit throat with knife According to Shashi Ranjan Mishra, he deeply loved his daughters but was worried about their future after his death. He said he planned to kill them and then commit suicide on 18 April. He mixed sleeping pills in their food. Once the girls became unconscious, he strangled them and later slit their throats with a sharp weapon. However, he said he could not gather the courage to end his own life. Family said - We have nothing to do with Shashi Ranjan Police officials from Naubasta station said Shashi Ranjan Mishra originally belonged to Gaya in Bihar, while his wife Reshma is from Siliguri in West Bengal. The couple had a love marriage in 2014 and lived in a rented flat. After the incident, Mishra’s father Shekhar Mishra, brother Rajeev Mishra, and sister Sweety clearly refused to come to Kanpur. They stated that he had married against the family’s wishes and they have no connection with him. They also refused to speak further and disconnected calls from police. Even when Reshma cried and informed them about the incident, they reportedly scolded her and disconnected the call. Reshma's family members will reach by this evening Reshma called her maternal family in West Bengal. Her mother and brother have left for Kanpur but are expected to arrive by Monday evening. On Sunday evening, Reshma reached the post-mortem house in a distressed condition, after which the post-mortem process began. Shashi Ranjan’s aunt Poonam from Varanasi arrived with her daughter Swashtika. Initially, the accused denied recognising them, but Reshma confirmed their identity. After this, police allowed them to meet her and attend the last rites at the Hindu burial ground. After the funeral, police helped Reshma sit in a vehicle and take her home. The relatives later left. Only Reshma and her son remained at the house. The entire apartment remained completely silent, with no one stepping out. Currently, two female police personnel have been deployed to look after Reshma. Riddhi-Siddhi used to wear clothes of the same color Riddhi and Siddhi shared a very close bond since birth. They always wore matching clothes and liked the same food. When their bodies were taken for cremation, neighbours also broke down. Their mother kept fainting repeatedly and kept calling out their names after regaining consciousness. My heart will find peace only when husband is hanged Reshma repeatedly broke down and said in front of police that only the death penalty for her husband would bring justice to her daughters and give her peace. Five witnesses not found, no one from family came Due to the accused’s difficult nature, 5 people were not found to sign the panchanama. Later, his domestic help Amravati alias Asha and his father were called to complete formalities. Both found with windpipes cut, death due to excessive bleeding A panel of three doctors conducted the post-mortem in the evening. It confirmed that both girls died due to excessive blood loss caused by deep throat injuries. Their windpipes were completely cut, and there were 3–4 inch deep wounds in the neck. Doctors said there was no chance of survival. Samples from the intestine and food (viscera) have been collected to check whether sleeping pills or any sedative substance was used. Had installed CCTV from kitchen to bedroom Reshma said she worked at a men’s salon in Kanpur where she met Shashi Ranjan Mishra. They married in 2014. Initially everything was fine, but later he started drinking and assaulting her regularly. She said he used to take sleeping pills and was highly suspicious. Because of this, he installed CCTV cameras from the entry gate to the kitchen and bedroom. She was not allowed to move freely inside the house, while the daughters stayed mostly with him. She added that she could enter the room only when he was out.

stories.title: Intense heatwave conditions grip Uttar Pradesh:26 districts cross 40°C; Banda ranks 3rd hottest in country
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh is witnessing intense heat conditions, with temperatures in 26 districts crossing 40°C. In the last 24 hours, Banda emerged as the third hottest city in the country, recording a maximum temperature of 44.6°C. On Friday, Banda was the hottest city in Asia, where the maximum temperature touched 45.4°C. This year, the heat has arrived nearly 10 days earlier than usual. Last year, temperatures first crossed 45°C on 27 April, while this year such conditions have already been recorded in mid-April. Due to rising temperatures, school timings for classes up to 8th standard have been changed in Varanasi and Prayagraj. Lucknow-based meteorologist Atul Singh said that due to an anti-cyclone system forming around Maharashtra, temperatures are expected to rise by 2–3°C over the next 2–3 days. Most districts may see temperatures reaching or crossing 45°C. Heatwave conditions are likely in parts of eastern Uttar Pradesh. There is currently no relief expected from the heat during the remaining days of April. Heatwave alert in Eastern UP The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued alerts for the night of 20 April. Warm nights are expected in Saharanpur, Muzaffarnagar, Bijnor, Moradabad, and Rampur. A heatwave warning has been issued for Firozabad, Banda, Chitrakoot, Kaushambi, Pratapgarh, Prayagraj, Mirzapur, Varanasi, Chandauli, and Sonbhadra. People have been advised to avoid direct sunlight and step out only if necessary, especially during afternoon hours. What will the weather be like for the next 4 days? Know- Nautapa Period Dates This Year This year, the Sun will enter Rohini Nakshatra on 25 May at 15:37. It will remain there until 8 June at 13:33, a period of 15 days. According to astrologer Puneet Vashney, the effect of ‘Nautapa’ will be felt during the first nine days of this period, from 25 May to 2 June. During this time, direct sunlight intensifies over the Earth, leading to extreme heat conditions. El Niño and La Niña explained El Niño: In this phenomenon, sea surface temperatures rise by 3–4°C. It occurs about twice in 10 years and disrupts rainfall patterns, causing low rainfall in high rainfall areas and vice versa. La Niña: In this case, sea waters cool rapidly. It impacts global weather patterns, leading to cloud formation and better rainfall in many regions. Why is it so hot already? According to meteorologists, due to the absence of any active weather system currently, dry westerly winds are directly reaching the plains. Along with this, an anti-cyclone formed over Karnataka and Maharashtra is now moving towards central India. This is causing a continuous rise in temperature.

stories.summary: The Yogi government on Sunday carried out a major administrative reshuffle in Uttar Pradesh, transferring 44 Additional Superintendents of Police (ASPs) across the state. Notably, 33 of these officers had recently been promoted from Deputy SP to Additional SP rank and have now been reassigned to new postings. Abhay Mishra has been transferred from the Vigilance department to Noida. Swayam Singh has also been posted in Noida after his promotion. Tanu Upadhyay has been appointed as Deputy Commandant in the 37th Battalion PAC in Kanpur. She was earlier serving as Assistant Commandant in the same unit. In 2025, she had also interviewed Infosys Foundation co-founder and BJP Rajya Sabha MP Sudha Murty regarding Mahakumbh arrangements. Shrestha Thakur appointed as ASP in ATS Lucknow Shrestha Thakur has been posted as ASP in ATS Lucknow. She is popularly known as “Lady Singham” and was earlier serving as ASP in Baghpat. Originally from Unnao, she cleared the UPPSC exam in 2012. She first came into the limelight in 2017 when she was CO in Bulandshahr, after a video of her heated argument with a political party worker over issuing a challan went viral. She was later transferred to Bahraich near the Nepal border. Sneha Tiwari becomes Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police Kanpur Sneha Tiwari has been given the responsibility of Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police (ADCP) in Kanpur Nagar Commissionerate. She is a 2012 batch PPS officer and originally belongs to Chunar in Mirzapur district. She started her service in 2014 with postings in Varanasi (Sadar and Dashashwamedh circles), later served in Jhansi and then Chandauli district. In Chandauli, she worked as DSP in the Sakaldiha area. She was recently promoted to ASP rank and played an important role in successfully implementing the Mission Shakti campaign in Chandauli, for which she was appreciated. Her husband is posted as an executive magistrate in Singrauli, Madhya Pradesh. See the complete list of who was sent where...

stories.title: Yogi govt transfers 40 IAS officers, 15 DMs:Shifts Kinjal Singh to education dept after face-off with minister
stories.summary: The Yogi Adityanath-led Uttar Pradesh government carried out a major administrative reshuffle late Sunday night, transferring 40 IAS officers, including 12 women officers, and changing postings across several key departments and districts. The exercise, finalised after prolonged internal deliberations within the state administration, also involved a large-scale reshuffle of District Magistrates (DMs) across 15 districts. Officials said the move aligns with administrative rotation norms and preparations ahead of future electoral requirements. Transport Commissioner Kinjal Singh has been removed and appointed as Secretary in the Secondary Education Department following reported differences with Transport Minister Dayashankar Singh and dissatisfaction over departmental functioning. She had taken charge only about seven months ago, having earlier served in several senior roles including Vice Chairman of Kanpur Development Authority, Director of Panchayati Raj, and Director General of Medical Education. Recently returned from central deputation, 2010-batch IAS officer Ashutosh Niranjan has been appointed as the new Transport Commissioner. Alok Kumar, Additional Chief Secretary of the Industrial Development Department, has been relieved of additional charge of the MSME and Export Promotion Department. The charge has been assigned to Shashi Bhushan Lal Sushil, Divisional Commissioner of Devipatan. Pankaj Kumar, Managing Director of Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Limited (UPPCL), has been removed after nearly five years in office amid the smart meter controversy and reported administrative differences involving senior officials, including the UPPCL Chairman and Energy Minister. He has not been assigned a new posting yet. Nitish Kumar, MD of Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam, has been appointed as the new MD of UPPCL. See the complete list of IAS officers' transfers- They reassigned charge of districts In a late-night administrative reshuffle, the Uttar Pradesh government reassigned several District Magistrates across key districts. Unnao District Magistrate Gaurang Rathi has been posted as DM Jhansi. Sultanpur DM Kumar Harsh has been made DM Bulandshahr. Shamli DM Arvind Kumar Chauhan has been appointed DM Saharanpur. Amroha DM Nidhi Gupta Vats has been transferred as DM Fatehpur. Hamirpur District Magistrate Ghanshyam Meena has been posted as DM Unnao. Mainpuri District Magistrate Anjani Kumar Singh has been made DM Lakhimpur Kheri. Auraiya DM Indramani Tripathi has been appointed DM Mainpuri. Saharanpur DM Manish Bansal has been posted as DM Agra. These officers get district charge for the first time The reshuffle also gave district charge to several IAS officers for the first time. Pankaj Kumar removed after five years Pankaj Kumar has been removed as Managing Director of Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation Limited (UPPCL) after serving since March 2021. A 2002-batch IAS officer, his removal comes amid the smart meter controversy and reported differences with UPPCL Chairman Ashish Goyal and Energy Minister Arvind Sharma. He has not been given a new posting so far. Nitish Kumar, Managing Director of Dakshinanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam, has been appointed as the new MD of Uttar Pradesh Power Corporation. Kinjal Singh removed after seven months Transport Commissioner Kinjal Singh has been removed from her post within seven months of appointment. She had taken charge on September 16, 2025. Differences with Transport Minister Dayashankar Singh and dissatisfaction over departmental functioning are cited as reasons. She has been posted as Secretary, Secondary Education Department, a move being seen within government circles as a sidelined assignment. Kinjal Singh has earlier held key positions, including Vice Chairman of Kanpur Development Authority, Director of Panchayati Raj, Director General of Medical Education, and Transport Commissioner. 2010-batch IAS officer Ashutosh Niranjan, recently returned from central deputation, has been appointed as the new Transport Commissioner. MSME charge withdrawn from Alok Kumar The charge of MSME and Export Promotion Department has been withdrawn from Additional Chief Secretary Alok Kumar. Officials indicated that excessive workload was affecting departmental functioning. Shashi Bhushan Lal Sushil, Divisional Commissioner of Devipatan, has been appointed Principal Secretary, MSME and Export Promotion Department. Other key administrative changes Chief Development Officers (CDOs) of five districts have also been changed, including Hapur, Sultanpur, Bahraich, Amethi, and Jhansi. In addition, several officers were moved to development authorities, universities, and departmental directorates. Major changes include: Background and administrative reasoning Officials said the reshuffle was driven by multiple factors, including completion of tenure in districts, administrative rotation norms, workload distribution, and preparation for future electoral processes requiring periodic reshuffling of district-level officers. Several long-serving officers were moved after completing more than two to three years in their respective postings. The exercise also aimed to create vacancies for first-time district postings for mid-level IAS batches (2014–2016). Key departmental reshuffle cases Transport Commissioner Kinjal Singh’s removal within seven months and Pankaj Kumar’s exit from UPPCL after five years were among the most notable changes in the exercise, both linked to internal administrative differences and departmental controversies.

Yogi cabinet expansion within 20 days, before 10 May:Focus on Brahmin, Dalit and women representation
stories.summary: The Yogi Adityanath government plans to complete its cabinet expansion by May 10. Meanwhile, the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) is restructuring the state organisation as part of preparations for the 2027 Assembly elections. The changes are being considered in consultation with Prime Minister Narendra Modi and RSS Joint General Secretary Arun Kumar, among other senior leaders. Discussions held in Lucknow to Delhi The Cabinet expansion plan was delayed due to BJP's organisational elections. Post these elections, state BJP chief Pankaj Chaudhary and general secretary Dharampal Singh discussed the Cabinet plan with central leaders on April 16-17. Currently, UP govt has 21 cabinet ministers, 14 ministers of state (independent charge), and 19 ministers of state. It can accommodate up to six more ministers. Focus on caste balance Brahmin representation: The BJP is looking to address concerns within the Brahmin community following recent controversies. At present, there are seven Brahmin ministers, including Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak. After Jitin Prasada moved to the Centre, a vacancy emerged. Sources indicate that two Brahmin leaders may be inducted. Dalit outreach: The party is also focusing on Dalit representation after signs of dissatisfaction during the 2024 Lok Sabha elections. Concerns included fears over reservation and representation. The government currently has eight ministers from Scheduled Castes, including Baby Rani Maurya. One or two more Dalit ministers may be added. Backward classes: Leaders from Other Backward Classes (OBCs) are also expected to be included. Among the likely names is former state BJP chief Bhupendra Chaudhary. Women’s representation likely to increase The BJP may induct more women ministers to strengthen its outreach among female voters. There are currently five women ministers in the state, while the Assembly has 51 women MLAs. Possible inclusion of SP rebels The BJP may also induct expelled Samajwadi Party (SP) leaders such as Manoj Pandey and Pooja Pal. The move is aimed at expanding social support among Brahmins, backward classes and women. Changes in BJP state unit Alongside the cabinet expansion, the BJP is finalising a new state team. A previous list was reportedly returned by Union Home Minister Amit Shah, who advised against major changes in an election cycle. A revised list is being prepared in consultation with senior leaders, including B. L. Santosh. Around 50% of current office-bearers are likely to be replaced, while some may be promoted. The cabinet expansion and organisational reshuffle are expected to reflect the BJP’s electoral strategy for 2027, with emphasis on caste balance, women’s representation and political outreach.

stories.title: CM Yogi says UP’s farm growth hits 18%:Record paddy and potato output; International Potato Centre to open in Agra
stories.summary: At a major agriculture conference in North India, Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said the state’s farm growth has more than doubled in recent years. He said the growth rate has risen from 8% to 18%, adding that farmers’ hard work and government policies have helped the state become a top producer of several crops. Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chauhan also attended the event held in Lucknow on April 24. The programme saw participation from agricultural scientists, farmer-producer groups, and progressive farmers from nine states and union territories. Lab technology now reached directly to the fields The Chief Minister said that earlier policies were limited only to papers and offices, but now 'lab to land', meaning laboratory technology, is being directly brought to the fields. He informed that in 2017, there were only 69 Krishi Vigyan Kendras (Agricultural Science Centers) in the state, most of which were about to close. Today, their number has increased to 89. These centers are now working as 'Centers of Excellence', where scientists themselves are going to farmers and providing them information about new techniques and seeds. Record Set in Paddy and Potato Production The Chief Minister stated through figures that currently, Uttar Pradesh is producing 425 lakh metric tons of wheat, 211 lakh metric tons of paddy, and 245 lakh metric tons of potatoes. Expressing happiness, he said that with the help of the International Rice Research Center in Varanasi, paddy yield in some areas of the state has now reached up to 100 quintals per hectare, which was very low earlier. Additionally, potato farmers will get even better prices for their crops from the International Potato Center, which will soon start in Agra. Focus on Value Addition for Economic Strength The Chief Minister emphasized the need to not limit farming to mere production but to connect it with the market and industry. He said that to increase agriculture's share in Uttar Pradesh's economy again, the government is now emphasizing 'value addition', i.e., the processing of products. This will not only prevent crop wastage but also enable farmers to get many times more value for their produce. The government's goal is to establish a strong synergy between manufacturing and agriculture, so that new employment opportunities can be created in rural areas themselves and farmers can establish their identity as entrepreneurs. 'Road Map' essential to increase farmers' income Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan praised Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath's work, stating that UP has created a new history of development. He emphasized that every state should prepare a 'road map' for farming according to its climate and soil. He informed that the work of creating 'Farmer IDs' is now progressing rapidly in the country, which will enable farmers to directly and easily avail the benefits of government schemes. The Chief Minister also expressed confidence that suggestions emerging from such conferences will bring significant changes in the lives of farmers. Every Farmer Will Have Their Own Digital Identity Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan specially emphasized the utility of 'Farmer ID' at the conference. He said that the central government is rapidly working on creating a unique digital identity for farmers across the country, which will save them from repeatedly going through paperwork. Through this ID, benefits of government schemes like fertilizers, seeds, and subsidies will reach their accounts directly and transparently. Praising the fertile land of UP and its hardworking farmers, he said that the soil and climate of the state are the basis of the country's food security, therefore, working by creating a solid 'Agriculture Road Map' according to the geographical conditions of each district is the need of the hour.
